CORAM : HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE RAJESH SHANKAR -----
For the Petitioners : Md. Kaisar Alam, Advocate For the State : A.C. to G.P.II

For Res. No.5 : Mrs. Sweety Topno, Advocate Bhuneshwar Sahu vs The State Of Jharkhand on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170192283/

Order No.04 Date: 19.01.2023 The present writ petition has been filed for quashing the order as contained in memo no.1534 dated 8th September, 2021 passed by the Additional Collector-cum-Arbitrator, Gumla- the respondent no.3 in Misc. Case nos.01, 02 & 03 of 2021-22, whereby, according to the petitioner, learned Arbitrator has erroneously assessed compensation @ Rs.10,030/- per decimal for acquisition of the land in question.

entities.text: Advocate Bhuneshwar Sahu vs The State Of Jharkhand
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
learned counsel appearing on behalf of the State respondents as well as learned counsel appearing for the respondent no.5 jointly raise preliminary objection with regard to maintainability of the writ petition and submit that the petitioner has got alternative/ statutory/efficacious remedy under Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 (hereinafter to be referred as 'the Act, 1996')
against the impugned order as contained in memo no.1534 dated 8th September, 2021 passed by the respondent no.3.

They also refer to the order dated 9th May, 2022 passed by this Court in W.P.(C)
No.4438 of 2021, operative part of which reads as under:-
"Since the respondent No.5 has raised an issue of maintainability of the present writ petition, it would be appropriate to deal with the said issue at the first instance.

Section 3-G(6) of the National Highways Act, 1956 [hereinafter referred to as 'the Act,
1956'] clearly provides that the provisions of the Act, 1996 shall apply to every arbitration under the said Act, subject to the other provisions of the same.

Thus, the impugned order as contained in memo No. 1611 dated 15.09.2021 passed by the respondent No.3 in Misc. Case No. 11/2021 has to be treated as an award passed within the meaning and the provisions of the Act, 1996.
The Act, 1956 does not provide any further Forum for challenging the award passed by an arbitrator under Section 3-G(5) of the said Act.

Thus, if any person is aggrieved with the award of an arbitrator passed under Section 3-G(5) of the Act, 1956, he has got the remedy to file an application under Section 34 of the Act, 1996 for setting aside the same."

Since, it has already been held by this Court in the order dated 9th May, 2022 that if any person is aggrieved with the award passed under Section 3-G(5) of the Act, 1956, he has got the remedy to file an application under Section 34 of the Act, 1996 for getting the same set aside, the present writ petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable and the same is, accordingly, dismissed as not maintainable.

The petitioner is, however, at liberty to take alternative/ statutory/efficacious recourse under Section 34 of the Act, 1996 against the impugned order as contained in memo no.1534 dated 8 th September, 2021 passed by the respondent no.3.

(Rajesh Shankar, J.) Sanjay/
